title: Animalia: Phyla Classification
notes: The organisms shown in the picture above are Euglena, Paramecium, Fuligo and Plasmodium respectively.
Euglena is a microscopic, unicellular and flagellate organism primariely found in freshwater.
Paramecium is also a microscopic and unicellular ciliate found in freshwater rich in decaying organc matter.
Fuligo is a fungi like unicellular organism which can be seen in decaying woods.
Similarly, Plasmodium is an intracellular blood parasite.

Euglena exhibits both autotrophic and heterotrophic mode of nutrition as it can prepare its own food and sometime derives food from other micro-organisms whereas Paramecium is a heterotrophic because it derives food from other microorganism or organic substances.
These organisms belong to the kingdom protista.
